COMPONENT-LIBRARY RESEARCH — MANDATORY

The project may use direct source inspection and compatible components from the following repositories:

- Untitled UI React: `https://github.com/untitleduico/react`
- shadcn/ui: `https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui`
- Magic UI: `https://github.com/magicuidesign/magicui`
- Motion Primitives: `https://github.com/ibelick/motion-primitives`
- React Bits: `https://github.com/DavidHDev/react-bits`
- coss UI and the legacy Origin UI directories: `https://github.com/cosscom/coss`
- Paper Shaders: `https://github.com/paper-design/shaders`

Use these as an extensive source catalogue for premium UI and interaction patterns.

Rules:

- Inspect licence and compatibility before copying.
- For coss, use only source whose applicable licence permits the intended use; the repository is mixed-licence.
- Pin Paper Shaders to an exact compatible version and preserve its required notice.
- Do not clone an entire external repository into tracked Silverstone source.
- Use a temporary checkout or inspect files remotely, then adapt only selected files.
- Do not import an entire package when one copied component is sufficient.
- Research several candidates for material component families such as navigation, hero, menus, carousels, forms and animated text.
- Combine accessible structural primitives from Untitled UI, shadcn or coss with visual/motion patterns from Magic UI, Motion Primitives, React Bits, Paper Shaders and the local component pack.
- Completely restyle all selected source.
- Do not produce a collage of unrelated templates.

Create and maintain:

`/docs/silverstone-redesign/component-source-ledger.md`

For every external or local source used, record:

- source library;
- source URL;
- exact file/component;
- commit, tag or package version where available;
- applicable licence;
- dependencies;
- why it was selected;
- how it was transformed;
- final Silverstone file path.

LOGO AND EMBLEM HANDLING — CRITICAL

The supplied `silverstone-icon.png`, `silverstone-logo-new.png` and `silverstone-logo-new@2x.png` contain white raster backgrounds.

Never place the raw image directly over a dark background in a way that produces an accidental white square or rectangle.

Retain all original files unchanged.

Use one or both of these deliberate treatments:

A. Light brand plate
- place the untouched image inside a deliberately designed Cloud White or Platinum Silver surface;
- use intentional geometry, padding, border, depth and lighting;
- make it visually obvious that the white area is a designed brand plate, not an unremoved image background.

B. Transparent derivative
- create a separate transparent-background derivative by removing only the contiguous white background;
- preserve exact geometry, metallic detail, internal cyan/blue/violet/pink light, typography, spelling, proportions and edges;
- do not redraw, recolour, regenerate or reinterpret the asset;
- use the 2x logo as the preferred high-resolution source;
- remove white halos without cutting metallic highlights;
- test on black, graphite, violet, white and checkerboard backgrounds at 100% and 200%;
- retain originals and use clearly named derivative files.

Header requirements:

- use the emblem on every page;
- on dark navigation, use an approved transparent derivative or an intentional light emblem plate;
- never substitute plain text for the emblem.

Footer requirements:

- use the full logo on every page;
- use an approved transparent derivative on dark surfaces or a clearly designed light logo panel;
- never show an accidental white rectangle.

ANIMATION MINIMUM — NON-NEGOTIABLE

Retain the existing React Router/Vite architecture. Do not migrate to Next.js.

Use compatible versions of:

- React;
- strict TypeScript;
- Tailwind CSS v4;
- shadcn/Radix or React Aria primitives;
- GSAP and ScrollTrigger;
- `@gsap/react`;
- Motion or Framer Motion, normalised to one package;
- Lenis;
- Three.js;
- React Three Fiber;
- Drei;
- React Three postprocessing;
- postprocessing;
- maath;
- Lucide React;
- Paper Shaders where selected;
- modern CSS and View Transitions.

GSAP owns page and scroll choreography.

Motion owns component state, menus, gestures and layout transitions.

CSS owns lightweight effects.

Never animate the same property on the same element using multiple systems.

Every major visible homepage section, heading, image, icon, metric, card, diagram and conversion element must have a deliberate entrance, state, hover or scroll behavior.

Use one signature WebGL hero and a controlled number of additional high-impact 3D moments. Do not put a heavy canvas behind every card.

Use Lenis without scroll-jacking and synchronise it with one GSAP loop.

Create reduced-motion, low-power and no-WebGL fallbacks that preserve all information.

PERFORMANCE AND QUALITY

- dynamically load heavy visual modules;
- cap DPR;
- lazy-load images and scenes;
- pause off-screen animation;
- dispose WebGL resources;
- avoid duplicate animation loops;
- use responsive images;
- eliminate hydration issues;
- avoid unexpected layout shift;
- ensure keyboard/touch/screen-reader access;
- maintain SEO crawlability;
- do not sacrifice the core visual experience merely to chase a perfect score.
